findings.message: When the monthly job finds an open standing allocation whose project is no longer active (or whose person is no longer active or joining), it only sets `until_month = filled_to + 1`. It leaves in place every month row the standing allocation already wrote, up to 12 months ahead. The leaver path in this same diff (`endStandingForLeaver` → `setStanding` with percent 0) deletes the rows from its end month on, so these are two rules for one class that disagree. Fix: end it through `setStanding(tx, { …, month: <the current month or the month after>, percent: 0 })` so the job removes rows the same way the leaver path does. Add the rows past the end to the standing-end-107 table test, which today checks only that the standing row is closed and that 2028-01 is missing.
findings.scenario: A standing allocation for Nimal on OLD at 30% from 2027-01 is written through 2027-12. OLD is closed, and the job runs on 2027-02-05 → the standing row is ended at 2028-01, but rows 2027-03…2027-12 at 30% stay in allocations.allocation. The capacity forecast and grid show Nimal 30% on a closed project for ten months, and the bench leaves them out.

findings.message: The allocate tool now always answers with the Add-to-project form for a project. On an internal project its `standing` chip defaults to "true" whenever the input has no `standing`, even when the request named a single month or a `through` range. The card has no field for `through`, so a range request becomes a refusal at confirm, and a single-month request becomes a 12-month standing allocation by default. Fix: default `standing` to true only when the input gives no `month` and no `through` (for example, `value: String(internal && !a.month && !a.through)`), and keep the range or give `through` a field when it is set.
findings.scenario: In chat: "allocate Kasun 40% to INT for 2026-12" → the model calls allocate({person, projectKey:'INT', month:'2026-12', percent:40}). The card preselects "Until further notice", and a person who presses Add gets a standing allocation written 2026-12…2027-11 instead of one month. The same request with through:'2027-02' is refused at confirm with "until further notice needs a project and no end month".

findings.message: Hand removals stay removed only for the monthly job. Re-setting a standing allocation brings them back. `skipMonths` stores a hand-removed month in the open standing row's `skip`. `setStanding` then ends or deletes that row and inserts a new one with `skip = '{}'`. `fill` writes all 12 months ahead again, including the month the person removed by hand. The same happens to hand removals inside `filled_to`, because `setAllocation` deleted that row and only `skip` remembers it. Fix: carry `skip` from the ended or dropped row into the new standing row for months >= `s.month`, and have `fill` leave those months out. Add a variant test that sets a standing allocation, removes a month by hand, then re-sets it at a new percent.
findings.scenario: Standing from 2026-10 at 50% → allocate 2027-03 percent 0 (removed by hand) → allocate standing 60% from 2026-12 → 2027-03 is back at 60%.

findings.message: There are now two definitions of 'today' in the add-person path, and they can disagree. The tool defaults `joinedOn` to `localToday` (the date in the entity's time zone). `addPerson` decides the status with `input.joinedOn > today()`, which uses the UTC date (`inforce.ts`). When the entity's date is already ahead of UTC, someone added today is stored as 'joining'. They then don't appear in the Add to project card's picks (`listPeople` with status active) until the daily job runs. Fix: use one entity-local date for both the default and the status check, for example by computing it in `addPerson` from the entity. Add a test with a clock set across the UTC date line for Sri Lanka and Australia.
findings.scenario: Add someone to the Sri Lanka entity at 2026-11-15T20:00Z → joinedOn 2026-11-16 > UTC today 2026-11-15 → status 'joining', and 'Add Priya Jayasena to CON' doesn't list them among the picks.
